flashcards.q: What does each edge and each root-to-node path represent in a trie?
flashcards.a: Each edge is one character; each root-to-node path spells a prefix of some inserted word.

flashcards.q: What field on a trie node distinguishes a complete word from a mere prefix, and what breaks if you forget it?
flashcards.a: An is_end boolean. Without it, search('ca') would incorrectly return true if only 'car' was ever inserted, since the path to 'ca' exists as a prefix.

flashcards.q: What is the time complexity of insert, search, and startsWith on a trie, and why is it independent of dictionary size?
flashcards.a: O(L) where L is the word/prefix length; each operation walks one path, one node per character, regardless of how many other words are stored.

flashcards.q: Why does a trie beat a hashmap for 'which words start with this prefix' queries?
flashcards.a: A hashmap has no relationship between a string and its prefixes, so it needs O(n*L) to scan all entries; a trie's shared-prefix subtree gives direct O(L) access to every matching word.

flashcards.q: When can a naive trie use MORE memory than a plain hashmap of the same strings?
flashcards.a: When the strings share little to no prefix overlap (e.g. random strings, UUIDs) — the per-node array/map overhead isn't offset by any prefix-sharing savings.

flashcards.q: How do you fix a trie's memory blowup while keeping prefix-query support?
flashcards.a: Compress chains of single-child nodes into one edge holding a substring instead of one node per character — a radix tree / Patricia trie.

flashcards.q: Word Search II (LC 212): why build a trie of the dictionary before DFS-ing the grid?
flashcards.a: One shared DFS pass over the grid, pruned by trie-child membership at every step, replaces running an independent search per dictionary word.

flashcards.q: Design Add and Search Words (LC 211): how does the '.' wildcard change trie search complexity?
flashcards.a: At a wildcard, branch into every existing child instead of following one path; worst case becomes O(26^k * L) for k wildcards, not O(L).
